Koç Holding stock highlights energy transition at COP31
sum: Koç Holding used its role as a global business partner of COP31 to put energy transition and industrial competitiveness at the center of its public message. At a panel held on November 10 in Antalya, Vice-Chair Ali Y. Koç said energy had moved beyond being a cost factor and had become decisive for global competition, according to PR Newswire.

Koç argued that governments are building domestic industrial capacity around energy independence and resilience. In his view, electrification and domestic clean-energy investment are becoming part of the competitive framework for industry rather than only climate-policy objectives.

He also called for COP31 to focus on investments mobilized, projects implemented and emissions reduced, rather than only on commitments. Koç proposed a scorecard covering both production capacity and the infrastructure needed to support the transition.

For investors, the remarks point to the importance of execution, financing and policy clarity across the group’s energy and industrial exposure. The statements do not provide new earnings guidance or a direct forecast for Koç Holding’s financial results, but they underline the strategic themes management is presenting during the conference.

Koç Holding’s investor-relations materials describe the group as a diversified Turkish conglomerate with activities in energy, automotive, consumer durables, finance and other businesses in Türkiye and international markets. Its energy operations include petroleum products, refining, fuel distribution and power generation, while its industrial portfolio includes vehicles and household appliances.
Broader sentiment for Turkish equities can be followed through the BIST 100 market environment.

items.t: Ali Y. Koç: 'The Energy Transition Has Become the Cornerstone of Competitiveness in Industry'
sum: At COP31's Highly Sensational Panel, the Impact of Climate Policies on Global Competition Was Discussed

As part of COP31 for which Koç Holding is a Global Business Partner, the panel discussion 'From Commitments to Action: The Role of Business and Policy in the Global Climate Agenda' was held. The event which began with an opening address by COP31 President Murat Kurum featured former US Vice-President Al Gore as keynote speaker.

Speaking at the panel moderated by IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol, Koç Holding Vice-Chair of the Board of Directors Ali Y. Koç said, "Energy has moved beyond being merely a cost factor in industry to becoming a decisive factor in global competition." Noting that governments are establishing domestic industrial infrastructures centred on energy independence and resilience, Koç affirmed that the essence of the energy transition lies in the widespread adoption of electrification and domestic clean energy investments.

ANTALYA, Türkiye, Nov. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As part of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) for which Koç Holding is as a Global Business Partner, the panel discussion 'From Commitments to Action: The Role of Business and Policy in the Global Climate Agenda' was held on 10 November. The event began with an opening address by Murat Kurum, Turkish Minister for the Environment, Urbanisation and Climate Change and President of COP31, and featured former US Vice-President Al Gore as keynote speaker. Following the speeches, a panel discussion took place, moderated by Dr. Fatih Birol, Executive Director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), whilst Ali Y. Koç, Vice-Chair of the Board of Directors of Koç Holding; Lei Zhang, Founder and CEO of Envision Energy; Oliver Bäte, CEO of Allianz; Odile Renaud-Basso, President of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD); and Greg Jackson, Founder and CEO of Octopus Energy, took part as panellists.

Congratulating Turkey on hosting COP31, former US Vice-President Al Gore said: "I would like to point out that we are fortunate to have all the technologies we need to reduce emissions. Tell future generations that we, who were alive in 2026, took action to fulfil our responsibilities.

Aygaz stock draws focus with nine-month LPG operating review
sum: Aygaz released an operating review for the first nine months of 2026, covering the period from January through September. The announcement was reported by TipRanks.

The review describes Aygaz as an LPG company that sources products domestically and internationally before distributing cylinder gas, bulk gas and autogas in Turkey. Its infrastructure at the end of September included five marine terminals, five filling facilities and eight distribution centers.

Aygaz's distribution system also included 1,912 cylinder-gas dealers and 2,004 autogas stations, according to the report. The figures underline the company's broad physical reach in a market where LPG remains an established fuel for households, commercial users and road transport.
Aygaz shares on Borsa Istanbul stood at 267.75 Turkish lira at 16:09 CET on Friday, November 6.
The report identified Koç Holding as Aygaz's largest shareholder, with a 40.68 percent stake. Publicly held shares represented 24.25 percent of issued capital.

Aygaz sources, stores, fills, distributes and delivers LPG products, including cylinder gas, bulk gas and autogas. It also manufactures cylinders, tanks, regulators, appliances and related equipment and provides after-sales services through its distribution network. The company's core market is Turkey, with operations spanning supply infrastructure, retail distribution and vehicle-fuel channels.

Turkey's LPG industry remains closely linked to the country's large autogas fleet and established refueling infrastructure. For investors, the operating review provides a snapshot of network scale and distribution capacity ahead of further financial reporting.

items.t: Singer to raise Tk 250cr through preference shares
sum: Singer Bangladesh Limited, a subsidiary of Beko, the flagship brand of Türkiye’s Koç Holding, plans to raise up to Tk 250 crore by issuing preference shares to refinance existing debt, lower its debt burden, and fund working capital.
The multinational home appliance maker will issue up to 25 crore preference shares at Tk 10 per share, the company said in a press statement yesterday.
The shares will be issued at the discretion of the issuer via private placement to the sponsor shareholder, subject to approval from the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission, Singer said.

The decision comes as the company reported an increased loss of Tk 77 crore for the July-September quarter of 2026, up from nearly Tk 48 crore in the same period a year ago. With the third-quarter earnings, Singer’s overall loss in the financial year 2026 stood at over Tk 119 crore, up 5 percent year-on-year, according to its financial statements.

Singer Bangladesh’s revenue, however, increased in the third quarter to Tk 440 crore, a 6.5 percent rise from the same period a year ago. In the first nine months of the year, it reported Tk 1,854 crore in sales, up from Tk 1,780 crore a year ago.
Singer said there was a gap between expectations and actual sales due to a stagnant consumer electronics market.
“Gross profit margins improved marginally, but increased cost of sales could not be fully passed on to consumers due to intense market price sensitivity,” said the company.

items.t: Koc Holding stock gets November 9 date for interim results
sum: Koç Holding will publish its interim financial reports for the period from January 1 through September 30, 2026, on November 9, according to a syndicated announcement carried by The Globe and Mail. The release will give investors the next broad reading on the Turkish group through the first three quarters of the year.

Koç Holding has also entered a two-week silent period before the disclosure. During that interval, the company does not comment on its financial position or hold meetings focused on financial matters, according to the announcement.

The scheduled release places the group’s automotive, energy, finance, industry and consumer businesses in focus. Investors will be watching how the portfolio performed through September and whether management provides fresh signals on operating conditions for the remainder of the year.

Koç Holding is a Turkish conglomerate with activities across industry, energy, automotive, finance and consumer services. The group is headquartered in Istanbul and operates through a broad portfolio of businesses serving the Turkish market and international operations. Its investor relations page provides access to financial information, presentations and company reports.

items.t: Sabanci Holding stock: E.ON venture plans 30-MW solar park
sum: A Sabanci-E.ON joint venture plans to build a 30-megawatt solar park with battery storage in Turkey, according to Renewables Now in a report published Monday, October 26, 2026. The announcement places Sabanci Holding's energy portfolio back in focus as investors assess the group's renewable-generation expansion.

The project combines solar generation with storage, potentially giving the joint venture greater flexibility in managing output. The report identifies Turkey as the project's market but does not provide a commissioning date, investment amount or ownership split.

For investors, the next milestones are construction progress, financing terms and the project's contribution to the group's energy capacity. The announcement is strategic rather than an immediate earnings update, so its financial effect will depend on execution and eventual operating performance.

Sabanci Holding's own investor-relations theme page lists nine-month results for November 4, 2026, following reported second-quarter net income of TRY 14.16 billion. That schedule gives investors a nearer-term point for assessing the performance of the holding's banking, energy, materials, financial-services and digital activities.

Simply Wall St describes Sabanci Holding as a Turkish group operating through subsidiaries in finance, manufacturing and trade at home and internationally. Its portfolio includes banking, energy, materials, financial services and digital operations. In Turkey's industrial-conglomerate peer group, Koç Holding and Anadolu Grubu Holding are named peers; Sabanci is differentiated by its broad exposure across financial and operating businesses rather than a single industrial niche.
Investors can follow the broader Turkish equity backdrop through current BIST 100 market coverage.

Turkish giant sponsoring COP31 cut climate goals then cashed in on oil boom
sum: When the Turkish COP31 presidency presented its priorities to international business leaders for the first time in New York in September, among those invited to give the private sector’s first response was Ali Koç, scion of one of Türkiye’s wealthiest families.

On stage, the vice chair of the board of Koç Holding said the family company, which weeks earlier had been announced as one of the top sponsors for the UN climate summit, can be seen as “quite exemplary” for its climate record.

What Koç did not mention was that the group’s biggest money-making arm - Türkiye’s largest oil refiner Tüpraş - plans to keep running its refineries “at maximum potential”. Nor did he say that, in 2025, both parent company and subsidiary cut their 2030 climate targets to a level they had already nearly achieved, as Climate Home News’ analysis of company records reveals.

The decision to hand Koç Holding a prominent role at COP31 - the company is also the summit’s "Global Business Partner" - has reignited a long-running controversy over the platforming of fossil fuel interests at the annual UN climate conference.

It has also thrown into question how COP sponsors are chosen and screened. The hosting agreement between the Turkish government and the UN climate secretariat (UNFCCC) says that a partner company’s “climate integrity” should be taken into account.

But how that test is applied is unclear and the process for picking sponsors remains largely opaque. The Turkish COP31 presidency has not published its selection criteria, nor the financial terms of any of its partnership agreements, including Koç’s. The UNFCCC declined to clarify how it advises on such deals.

Campaigners have long argued that accepting sponsorship from polluting companies is wrong because it gives them a global stage, visibility and access to policymakers at talks that are meant to move the world away from fossil fuels, and tarnishes the reputation of the COPs.

items.t: Türkiye's BIST 100 shatters record as banking stocks power past 14,000
sum: Türkiye's benchmark stock index shattered its all-time record on Thursday, blowing past the 14,000-point barrier for the first time in its history as a rally in banking shares and growing confidence in the central bank's inflation strategy fueled broad-based buying across the market.

The Borsa Istanbul BIST 100 index closed at 14,180.48 points, a gain of 392.66 points or 2.85 percent from the previous session. The index touched an intraday high of 14,196.85 before pulling back slightly into the close. The BIST 30, which tracks the exchange's largest companies, posted an even stronger session, surging 3.89 percent to finish at 15,684.58.

The breakout capped a remarkable start to the year for Turkish equities. The BIST 100 opened 2025 at 11,261.52 points and finished January at 13,838.29, delivering returns of nearly 23 percent in a single month, its best January performance since 1997. The buying momentum has carried into February with no signs of slowing.

Thursday's gains were led decisively by the banking sector, whose index jumped 6.96 percent on the session, far outpacing every other industry group. The financial sector index rose 3.06 percent, while industrials gained 2.61 percent, technology added 2.49 percent, and services climbed 1.44 percent. Of the 100 stocks in the benchmark, 93 closed higher and only five declined. Turkish Airlines, Turkiye Is Bankasi, Akbank, Koc Holding, and Sasa Polyester were among the most actively traded names.

Total trading volume on the exchange reached 274.6 billion liras, roughly $6.3 billion, underscoring the breadth of participation in the rally. The total market capitalization of the BIST 100 stood at approximately 14 trillion liras, or $322.3 billion.

The catalyst for Thursday's breakout was the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye's inflation report briefing, where Governor Fatih Karahan laid out a set of forecasts that analysts interpreted as a signal the bank would maintain a cautious approach to monetary easing.

Karahan told reporters that the bank projects inflation will fall to between 15 and 21 percent in 2026, declining further to a range of 6 to 12 percent by the end of 2027. The interim inflation targets were kept at 16 percent for 2026 and 9 percent for 2027, with a new 2028 interim target set at 8 percent.
